title: Who Do You Follow?
summary: In a war of information, don't hand spiritual authority to people you can't know. Look at their lives, and be under godly leadership in a local church.
exhortation: This passage gives us a path out of sin and into Jesus. But the focus I want to bring this morning is on evaluating authority, especially online authority. How do we know who to follow? I felt like God put this on my heart because we live in a war of information. It feels like the Wild West right now, a fire hose of information from every direction. Who do we trust? What do we take in and what do we tune out? How do we know who is a genuine Christian?

Two stories. In the group of churches I'm part of, there was a young man, Josh Harris, who was an excellent preacher and a talented leader, and I think he was genuine in his day. Then he walked away from the Lord and left his marriage and his faith. It was a puzzle to me. How do I evaluate this, and what do I learn from it? And most people know of Ravi Zacharias, who spoke the truth powerfully and eloquently, and it turned out he was living in sexual immorality.

So what do we do with that? We don't just look at someone's ministry and eloquence. We look at their life, as this passage says: "Whoever says 'I know him' but does not keep his commandments is a liar, and the truth is not in him." Do they live a life of repentance? Do they keep the Lord's commandments?

One of the best protections is to be in a local church, under godly leadership in a personal, local way. You can't depend on the online space. That's a fool's errand. And in Christianity there are no secrets. We all have God's word. Someone online can speak the truth, and there is help to be had there, but we aren't following those people, and we can't give them authority, because we can't know them. That's what the local church is for. Listen to your pastor, and if you don't have one, you should. How do you evaluate a pastor? Not first by his preaching or personality, but by his character. You should be able to know that he is a man of high character. And at the end of the day, the truth is the truth. A leader who falls into sin doesn't change it.
prayer: Lord, show us if we are putting any human authority in a place only you should sit. Be the great Shepherd of our lives. Help us find the community you designed for us: a body of believers, a church to plug into, and a pastor we can submit to and be led by. Keep us from becoming doomers who have given up on community, people and church. Help us press into what you have for us, so that we grow, are sanctified and build relationships, even when we've been hurt. Where it stings, bring healing, and if fellowship has been lost, help us know it again.

Help us build your church. Help us live humble lives, without controversy for its own sake, living quietly for you, Jesus, with an immovable boldness that doesn't veer from the truth. We pray this in Jesus' name. Amen.
